overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear viewer preference for 'What If' scenarios combined with extreme space anomalies and planetary extremes (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y with 1024 views and 38 likes, 8KEl0_pJ_68 with 972 views). Traditional straightforward facts perform moderately well, but interactive hypothetical space questions and high-stakes planetary concepts consistently yield the highest engagement rates (likes-per-view) over the recent 7-day window.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed standard declarative facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster and extreme planetary immersion hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') to drive high engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1026 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes) show strong pull for bizarre, hyper-visual physics.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing 19-21 second shorts focusing on surreal extraterrestrial weather and materials.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) failed to gain traction compared to heavy space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychology trivia unless structured as an interactive 'What If' or high-stakes challenge.

weak_patterns.pattern: Ultra-Short Run-times (<15s) Without High Visual Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: 12-15 second clips on common animal facts (e.g., Octopuses Have Three Hearts variants) underperformed relative to the 19-21 second immersive space scenarios.
weak_patterns.action: Ensure all future shorts maintain a solid 19-21 second duration to allow proper narrative arc and higher retention.
